feedback.finish: The Romans came from the city of Rome, which is the modern-day capital of Italy.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: After Rome was founded in 754 BC, the city continued to grow. Throughout the centuries, the Romans expanded their territory by winning wars and forming alliances. The Romans called their newly acquired areas provinces.

Over time, Rome developed from a small city into the capital of the Roman Empire, which stretched across parts of Europe, North Africa and the Middle East. In Latin, this empire was called the Imperium Romanum.

atoms.a: What did the Romans call the areas they acquired in their conquest?
What is the Latin name for the Roman Empire?

instruction.text: Select the three main things the Romans took during their conquests.

feedback.finish: As the Roman Empire was so large, it was very expensive to run. Valuable items helped, but the most common way of making money was selling prisoners into slavery.

instruction.text: Select the image you think shows Roman life.

feedback.finish: Unlike in Britain at the time, the Romans used silver coins showing their leader’s face.
Rome had a senate, where politicians could give speeches and citizens could pass votes.

atoms.b: Over 2,000 years ago, Rome already had hundreds of thousands of ((++people pigeons)) living there. It was a big city, and very ((++advanced advent)), with large temples and even its own sewer system.

In order to create ((food ++space)) for all these people, the Romans focused on increasing the ((width ++height)) of their buildings — sometimes as high as 6 storeys! This was extremely rare for the time, and made Rome one of the most developed cities in the world.
